# World population trends and CO₂ emissions

This project explores global population patterns and country-level carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. It includes data inspection, cleaning, missing-value treatment, descriptive analysis, visualizations, correlation analysis, regression, and continental comparisons.

## Setup and package loading

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```

## Data cleaning and missing-value treatment

```{r}
# Remove duplicate rows and, if identical, the extra 2019 CO2 column.
population_clean <- unique(population_raw)
co2_clean <- unique(co2_raw)

if ("X2019.1" %in% names(co2_clean)) {
  if (identical(co2_clean$X2019, co2_clean$X2019.1)) {
    co2_clean$X2019.1 <- NULL
  }
}

co2_years <- 1990:2019
co2_columns <- paste0("X", co2_years)

# Fill only short gaps between known CO2 values.
# Longer gaps and missing values at the beginning or end of a series remain missing.
fill_short_gaps <- function(values, max_gap = 2) {
  values <- as.numeric(values)
  known_positions <- which(!is.na(values))

  if (length(known_positions) < 2) {
    return(values)
  }

  estimated_values <- approx(
    x = known_positions,
    y = values[known_positions],
    xout = seq_along(values),
    rule = 1
  )$y

  missing_positions <- which(is.na(values))

  if (length(missing_positions) == 0) {
    return(values)
  }

  missing_groups <- split(
    missing_positions,
    cumsum(c(1, diff(missing_positions) != 1))
  )

  for (group in missing_groups) {
    is_short_gap <- length(group) <= max_gap
    is_between_known_values <- (
      min(group) > min(known_positions) &&
      max(group) < max(known_positions)
    )

    if (is_short_gap && is_between_known_values) {
      values[group] <- estimated_values[group]
    }
  }

  values
}

co2_interpolated <- co2_clean

co2_interpolated[co2_columns] <- t(
  apply(co2_clean[co2_columns], 1, fill_short_gaps)
)

missing_before <- sum(is.na(co2_clean[co2_columns]))
missing_after <- sum(is.na(co2_interpolated[co2_columns]))
estimated_count <- missing_before - missing_after

cat("Missing annual CO2 values before interpolation:", missing_before, "\n")
cat("Missing annual CO2 values after interpolation:", missing_after, "\n")
cat("Values estimated through interpolation:", estimated_count, "\n")
```

## Outlier analysis

```{r}
population_numeric <- population_clean[
  sapply(population_clean, is.numeric)
]

# Rank represents position, not a measured quantity, so it is excluded.
population_numeric$Rank <- NULL

outlier_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(population_numeric),
  Potential_outliers = sapply(
    population_numeric,
    function(values) length(boxplot.stats(values)$out)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  outlier_summary,
  caption = "Potential population outliers based on the IQR rule"
)

for (variable in names(population_numeric)) {
  print(
    ggplot(population_numeric, aes(y = .data[[variable]])) +
      geom_boxplot(
        fill = "lightblue",
        outlier.color = "firebrick"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Population data:", variable),
        x = NULL,
        y = variable
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  )
}
```

## CO₂ emissions distribution

```{r}
ggplot(co2_clean, aes(y = X2019)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "lightgreen",
    na.rm = TRUE,
    outlier.color = "firebrick"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "CO2 emissions per person in 2019",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Metric tons per person"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Descriptive statistics

```{r}
area_column <- grep("^Area", names(population_clean), value = TRUE)[1]
density_column <- grep("^Density", names(population_clean), value = TRUE)[1]

summary(
  population_clean[
    c(
      "X2022.Population",
      area_column,
      density_column,
      "Growth.Rate",
      "World.Population.Percentage"
    )
  ]
)

summary(co2_clean$X2019)
```

## Population projection for 2030

```{r}
# This assumes the annual growth rate stays constant from 2022 to 2030.
population_2022 <- population_clean$X2022.Population
annual_growth_rate <- log(population_clean$Growth.Rate)
years_to_2030 <- 8

population_clean$Population_2030 <- round(
  population_2022 * exp(annual_growth_rate * years_to_2030)
)

knitr::kable(
  head(
    population_clean[
      ,
      c(
        "Country.Territory",
        "X2022.Population",
        "Population_2030"
      )
    ],
    15
  ),
  caption = "Estimated 2030 population for the first 15 countries"
)
```

## Ten most populous countries

```{r}
top_ten <- head(
  population_clean[
    order(-population_clean$X2022.Population),
  ],
  10
)

knitr::kable(
  top_ten[
    ,
    c("Country.Territory", "X2022.Population")
  ],
  caption = "Ten most populous countries in 2022"
)

ggplot(
  top_ten,
  aes(
    x = reorder(Country.Territory, X2022.Population),
    y = X2022.Population
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Ten most populous countries in 2022",
    x = "Country",
    y = "Population"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Population trends over time

```{r}
population_years <- c(1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2022)

population_long <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    population_years,
    function(year) {
      data.frame(
        Country = top_ten$Country.Territory,
        Year = year,
        Population = top_ten[[paste0("X", year, ".Population")]]
      )
    }
  )
)

ggplot(
  population_long,
  aes(
    x = Year,
    y = Population,
    color = Country,
    group = Country
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = population_years) +
  labs(
    title = "Population trends in the ten most populous countries",
    subtitle = "Lines connect the available benchmark years",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Population",
    color = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Combining population and CO₂ datasets

```{r}
merged_data <- merge(
  population_clean,
  co2_clean,
  by.x = "CCA3",
  by.y = "country_code",
  all.x = TRUE
)

merged_interpolated <- merge(
  population_clean,
  co2_interpolated,
  by.x = "CCA3",
  by.y = "country_code",
  all.x = TRUE
)

unmatched_count <- sum(
  is.na(merged_data$X1990) &
    is.na(merged_data$Country.Name)
)

cat(
  "Population rows without a matching CO2 country code:",
  unmatched_count,
  "\n"
)
```

## CO₂ emissions trends

```{r}
co2_top_ten <- merged_data[
  merged_data$CCA3 %in% top_ten$CCA3,
]

co2_long <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    co2_years,
    function(year) {
      data.frame(
        Country = co2_top_ten$Country.Territory,
        Year = year,
        CO2_per_person = co2_top_ten[[paste0("X", year)]]
      )
    }
  )
)

ggplot(
  co2_long,
  aes(
    x = Year,
    y = CO2_per_person,
    color = Country,
    group = Country
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "CO2 emissions per person in the ten most populous countries",
    subtitle = "Missing observations are shown as gaps, not zeros",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Metric tons per person",
    color = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Interpolation assessment

```{r}
observed_top_ten <- co2_clean[
  co2_clean$country_code %in% top_ten$CCA3,
]

interpolated_top_ten <- co2_interpolated[
  co2_interpolated$country_code %in% top_ten$CCA3,
]

cat(
  "Missing top-ten country-year values before interpolation:",
  sum(is.na(observed_top_ten[co2_columns])),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Missing top-ten country-year values after interpolation:",
  sum(is.na(interpolated_top_ten[co2_columns])),
  "\n"
)
```

## Correlation analysis

```{r}
correlation_columns <- c(
  area_column,
  density_column,
  "Growth.Rate",
  "World.Population.Percentage"
)

correlation_matrix <- cor(
  population_clean[correlation_columns],
  use = "complete.obs"
)

knitr::kable(
  round(correlation_matrix, 3),
  caption = "Pearson correlations among population characteristics"
)

correlation_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(correlation_matrix))
names(correlation_long) <- c("Variable_1", "Variable_2", "Correlation")

ggplot(
  correlation_long,
  aes(
    x = Variable_1,
    y = Variable_2,
    fill = Correlation
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Correlation)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "firebrick",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlations among population characteristics",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Correlation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))
```

## Population and CO₂ relationship

```{r}
paired_data <- merged_data[
  complete.cases(
    merged_data[
      ,
      c("X2022.Population", "X2019")
    ]
  ),
]

cat("Countries included in the comparison:", nrow(paired_data), "\n")
cat(
  "Pearson correlation:",
  cor(paired_data$X2022.Population, paired_data$X2019),
  "\n"
)
cat(
  "Spearman correlation:",
  cor(
    paired_data$X2022.Population,
    paired_data$X2019,
    method = "spearman"
  ),
  "\n"
)

population_co2_model <- lm(
  X2019 ~ X2022.Population,
  data = paired_data
)

summary(population_co2_model)

ggplot(
  paired_data,
  aes(x = X2022.Population, y = X2019)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE,
    color = "firebrick"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "2022 population and 2019 CO2 emissions per person",
    x = "Population in 2022",
    y = "CO2 emissions in 2019 (metric tons per person)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Regression diagnostics and comparison

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(population_co2_model, which = 1)
plot(population_co2_model, which = 2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

paired_interpolated <- merged_interpolated[
  complete.cases(
    merged_interpolated[
      ,
      c("X2022.Population", "X2019")
    ]
  ),
]

cat(
  "Pearson correlation using observed CO2 values:",
  cor(paired_data$X2022.Population, paired_data$X2019),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Pearson correlation using interpolated CO2 values:",
  cor(
    paired_interpolated$X2022.Population,
    paired_interpolated$X2019
  ),
  "\n"
)
```

## Continental comparison

```{r}
# These summaries are not total continental emissions.
continent_sum <- aggregate(
  X2019 ~ Continent,
  data = paired_data,
  sum
)

continent_mean <- aggregate(
  X2019 ~ Continent,
  data = paired_data,
  mean
)

continent_count <- aggregate(
  X2019 ~ Continent,
  data = paired_data,
  length
)

continent_summary <- Reduce(
  function(first, second) merge(first, second, by = "Continent"),
  list(continent_sum, continent_mean, continent_count)
)

names(continent_summary) <- c(
  "Continent",
  "Sum_of_country_values",
  "Mean_of_country_values",
  "Countries_observed"
)

continent_summary <- continent_summary[
  order(-continent_summary$Sum_of_country_values),
]

knitr::kable(
  continent_summary,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Country-level CO2-per-person indicators by continent in 2019"
)

ggplot(
  continent_summary,
  aes(
    x = reorder(Continent, Sum_of_country_values),
    y = Sum_of_country_values
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Sum of country-level CO2-per-person values by continent",
    subtitle = "This is not a measure of total continental emissions",
    x = "Continent",
    y = "Sum of country-level values"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

cat("Highest value:", continent_summary$Continent[1], "\n")
cat(
  "Third-highest value:",
  continent_summary$Continent[3],
  "—",
  continent_summary$Sum_of_country_values[3],
  "\n"
)
cat(
  "Lowest value:",
  tail(continent_summary$Continent, 1),
  "—",
  tail(continent_summary$Sum_of_country_values, 1),
  "\n"
)
```
